upsertSlices.label: Adjacency-list LCA membership
upsertSlices.task: Answer consistent vertex-membership queries for one maximal independent set
assumptions: Adjacency-list access
Maximum degree Δ; n vertices
Randomized, high probability

results.bound: poly(Δ) · log n; Neighbor probes per membership query
results.guarantee: Exact maximal independent set; Consistent YES/NO membership in one maximal independent set
results.sourceLocation: Theorems 1.1 and 2.16; Section 1.1 defines the shared-tape adjacency-list model
results.notes: The expected cost for a fixed queried vertex is poly(Δ), retained separately. The exponent of Δ is unspecified and is never assigned a numeric coordinate.
assumptions: n is the vertex count; Δ is the maximum degree
The input graph is fixed before the random tape
Membership refers to a maximal independent set, not a maximum independent set
results.oracle: Adjacency-list neighbor probes: (v,i) returns the ith neighbor
results.probability: For each fixed v and η>0, poly(Δ) log(1/η) probes suffice with probability ≥1−η. Setting inverse-polynomial η and union bounding gives the high-probability all-vertex budget.
results.output: Consistent YES/NO membership in one maximal independent set

results.guarantee: Exact maximal independent set; Consistent YES/NO membership in one maximal independent set
results.sourceLocation: Corollary 11; Section 2.2 defines CentLocal probes and statelessness
results.notes: The full degree-sensitive bound is Δ^{O(Δ²)} · log* n. This panel fixes Δ, so the result is O(log* n). No polynomial-in-Δ claim is made.
assumptions: Distinct vertex IDs; known n and maximum degree bound Δ
Δ is held fixed for the displayed n-dependence
Deterministic, stateless: no state retained between membership queries
Membership refers to a maximal independent set, not a maximum independent set
results.oracle: Adjacency-list neighbor probes; the source also returns a reverse port, simulable with at most Δ neighbor probes
results.output: Consistent YES/NO membership in one maximal independent set

results.notes: The source explicitly transfers its Table 1 LOCAL lower bounds to deterministic query-order-oblivious CentLOCAL. For fixed Δ, strong and single-neighbor probes differ by only a constant factor. This pairs with the stateless upper bound in n, not in Δ.
assumptions: Fixed degree bound
Deterministic and query-order oblivious; no claim for arbitrary stateful randomized LCAs
Probe locations may be nonlocal
The stronger full-neighbor probe lower bound also applies to single-neighbor probes
results.oracle: Lower bound permits strong probes revealing all neighbors of any chosen vertex
results.probability: Deterministic correctness on all valid inputs and queries
results.output: Consistent YES/NO membership in one maximal independent set

upsertSlices.label: Erdős–Rényi joint graph and MIS access
upsertSlices.task: Generate consistent access to a sampled random graph and one MIS
assumptions: The graph is sampled as G(n,q), with q the edge probability; n is the number of vertices
Joint local access generator and LCA; not worst-case arbitrary input
Sampling within n^{−c} total variation of G(n,q); memoryless on a fixed random tape

results.bound: polylog(n) / q; Work per graph-edge or MIS-membership query
results.guarantee: A sampled graph together with one exact MIS; Joint graph adjacency answers and MIS membership answers
results.notes: The near-G(n,q) sampling guarantee from Definition 1.11 is part of the theorem contract. The theorem supplies a work bound, not an input-adjacency-probe bound. No comparable lower bound is verified in this source set.
assumptions: q is the edge probability (called p in the source)
Graph and MIS are generated together
No assertion for a fixed adversarial graph
For q≥1/polylog(n), the work simplifies to polylog(n)
results.oracle: Local Access Generator: the graph is generated by the oracle, not supplied as a fixed input
results.probability: Per-query complexity holds with high probability; generated graph distribution is within n^{−c} total variation of G(n,q), for desired constant c
results.output: Joint graph adjacency answers and MIS membership answers
